coordinates: pixels in the full scan above, origin top left
method: Each lateral frame cropped from the full scan at 1.2-2.2x with a grid labelled in scan pixels and raised contrast. Points picked by eye: head = eye or beak base (pigeon: eye; vulture: eye/beak base where the head is not covered by the wing); shoulder = where the near wing's leading edge leaves the back; wingTip = the most distal primary of the near wing; tailTip = end of the tail. All points were drawn back onto the crops (body line head->tail, wing line shoulder->tip) and checked; points that did not sit on the feature were moved or dropped. Angles use image coordinates with y up. bodyPitchDeg: angle of the tail->head line above the horizontal (nose up positive). wingElevationDeg: angle of the shoulder->wingTip line measured from the body's rearward axis (head->tail), positive toward the back (dorsal): 0 = wing lying back along the body, +90 = straight up from the back, +/-180 = pointing forward, -90 = straight down. These are side-view (projected) angles: a wing pointing toward the camera foreshortens, so projected length is recorded too. Wingbeat period comes from the frame lag at which the wing silhouette repeats (phase matching across the plate), times the catalogue interval. Frames where the head or tail is hidden get points but no angle. Vulture faces right. The lateral frames are small, so most points are low confidence and only frames with an identifiable head and tail get angles.

timing.cyclesSource: muybridge-1887-catalogue (fraction of a cycle shown on the plate)
timing.observedComputed: the silhouette repeats 7 frames later (1~8, 2~9, 3~10, 4~11, 5~12): 7 x 40 ms = 280 ms; +/-1 frame gives 3.1-4.2 Hz. This puts about 1.6 cycles on the plate.

downstrokeShare.computed: top at frames 6-7, wing lowest at frames 3-4 / 10-11, flexed upstroke at 5 / 12: about 3.5 intervals down, 3.5 up, of 7. At 40 ms sampling this is coarse.

wingElevationDeg.computed: near wing, frames 6-7 (top) and 2, 9 (wing reaching ahead of the head)

findings: Wingbeat about 3.6 Hz (7 frames at 40 ms by phase matching), agreeing with plate 765 (3.8 Hz at 19 ms). The catalogue fraction (1 1/4) would give 2.8 Hz.

The downstroke starts with the wing thrown far forward, past the beak (frames 1, 8), then sweeps down and back beneath the body (frames 3-4, 10-11); the upstroke is made with the wing flexed (5, 12). At the top the near wing points up and back (+58 to +68 deg from the rearward body axis).
Compared with figures/goose.json: as for plate 765, the goose wing (+26 to +76 deg) matches the top of this stroke but never reaches forward or below the body; frequency 6-7 Hz vs 3.6 Hz here.
Not measured: frames 1, 3-5, 10-12 angles (head hidden or near/far wing ambiguous); body bob (frames too small, and the plate-768 backdrop lines were not traced); the rear views.
